answer: A stake bond makes fake identities expensive: every agent locks a refundable deposit before it can transact, and the bond is slashed if peers prove it spawned sock-puppets. One real agent is a single vertex in the trust graph; a sybil farm must fund a deposit at every vertex, so its cost scales linearly while its gain stays flat. Like an ocean, the honest economy is deep — but a hollow identity with no stake behind it cannot bid, vote, or earn. It simply has no weight.
